question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate Meta Platforms' capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, for the third quarter of 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), in US dollars, as it will be first reported in Meta's third-quarter 2026 earnings press release.

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: Q2 2026 actual capex ($31.08B) grown by a Q3 step-up factor calibrated to historical Q3/Q2 ratios and the FY guidance-implied H2 ramp. p120.role: Meta H1 2026 capex including finance-lease principal ($50.92B), used with FY guidance to derive H2

methods.rationale: Guidance route: FY2026 guidance midpoint ($137.5B, from p120 range $130-145B) minus H1 actual ($50.92B) gives H2 total; multiplied by Q3 share (a2). Note formula uses p120 as H1 actual and doubles it as a proxy for the FY midpoint — this is a simplification; the true FY midpoint is $137.5B vs 2×$50.92B=$101.84B, so this formula understates. Intended as a directional cross-check only; the dominant method is m1.

assumptions.name: Q3 2026 sequential capex growth factor over Q2 2026
assumptions.rationale: Historical Q3 step-ups: Q3 2025 $19.37B vs Q2 2025 $17.01B = 1.14x; Q3 2024 vs Q2 2024 also rose. With FY2026 guidance $130-145B and H1 $50.92B, H2 must average ~$40-47B/quarter, implying Q3 well above Q2's $31.08B. A 1.12x factor (Q3 ~$34.8B) sits between the modest historical step-up and the aggressive consensus ($40.97B); range spans 1.02x to 1.30x to cover both.
assumptions.applies_when: Q3 2026 capex follows the historical pattern of sequential increases with a Q3 step-up, tempered by the FY guidance-implied H2 ramp.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Q3 2026 capex is flat or declining vs Q2, or that consensus ~$41B is confirmed by multiple independent sources.

assumptions.name: Q3 share of H2 2026 capex
assumptions.rationale: Historically Q3 is slightly below Q4 in H2 capex (Q3 2025 $19.37B vs Q4 2025 implied ~$22-23B from FY $70-72B and 9M ~$48.3B PP&E). A ~48% Q3 share of H2 is consistent; range covers 42-54%.

assumptions.falsified_by: Guidance commentary indicating Q3-weighted or Q4-weighted H2 phasing.

Anchored on p1; the growth factor a1 is centered slightly above the historical ~1.14x Q3 step-up given the steeper 2026 ramp, but below the ~1.30x implied by consensus. Failure mode: if the AI buildout causes a step-change beyond historical seasonality, this understates.

p120.role: Meta H1 2026 capex including finance-lease principal ($50.92B), used with FY guidance to derive H2

methods.rationale: Guidance-implied route: FY2026 guidance midpoint (~$137.5B) minus H1 actual ($50.92B) gives H2 capex; multiply by Q3's historical share of H2. Uses p120 and a2. Failure mode: guidance range is wide ($130-145B) and the Q3/Q4 split is uncertain; a Q4 back-end load would lower the estimate.

p64.role: Meta Q3 2025 capex including finance-lease principal ($19.37B), the year-ago base

a3.role: Q3 2026 capex as a multiple of Q3 2025 capex

methods.rationale: YoY-growth route: apply a YoY multiple to Q3 2025 capex. The multiple a3 is centered near 2.0x, consistent with the FY2026 guidance-implied growth (~1.8-2.0x) and the ~$40B consensus (~2.1x). Failure mode: if YoY growth decelerates or accelerates materially from the full-year trajectory, this misses.

p157.role: Analyst consensus Q3 2026 capex including finance leases ($40.5B, S&P Global Market Intelligence)

methods.rationale: Consensus route: use the S&P Global Market Intelligence consensus figure ($40.5B) directly. This is the most credible single consensus point (better provenance than the zhenzhuo $40.97B). Failure mode: consensus may embed an acceleration that does not materialize, or may be stale; it conflicts with the base-rate trajectory (~$33-36B).

assumptions.name: Q3 2026 sequential capex growth factor over Q2 2026
assumptions.rationale: Historical Q3 step-ups over Q2 for Meta capex have been roughly 10-15% (Q3 2025 $19.37B vs Q2 2025 $17.01B ≈ 1.14x). The 2026 ramp is steeper, so center slightly above the historical norm but below the ~1.30x implied by the ~$40B consensus, reflecting uncertainty about whether the acceleration is real.
assumptions.applies_when: Q3 2026 capex continues the sequential-increase pattern seen in prior years without a step-change beyond historical Q3 seasonality.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Q3 2026 capex jumped ~30% sequentially (matching the ~$40B consensus) or that it plateaued at Q2 levels.

assumptions.name: Q3 share of H2 2026 capex
assumptions.rationale: Historically Q3 has been roughly 48-50% of H2 capex (Q3 2025 $19.37B vs H2 2025 implied ~$40B). Centered at 0.48 with a range reflecting the possibility of a Q4-weighted back-end load.
assumptions.applies_when: H2 2026 capex is split between Q3 and Q4 in roughly the historical proportion.
assumptions.falsified_by: Guidance commentary or supplier signals indicating a strong Q4 back-end load (Q3 share well below 0.42) or front-loading (above 0.54).

assumptions.name: Q3 2026 capex as multiple of Q3 2025 capex
assumptions.rationale: Q2 2026 capex grew 83% YoY; the FY2026 guidance ($130-145B) vs FY2025 (~$72B) implies roughly 1.8-2.0x full-year growth. Q3 2026 YoY multiple centered near 2.0x, consistent with the guidance trajectory and the ~$40B consensus (~2.1x Q3 2025's $19.37B).
assumptions.applies_when: Q3 2026 YoY capex growth is in line with the full-year guidance-implied growth rate.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that YoY growth decelerated sharply below ~1.75x or accelerated above ~2.35x.

methods.label: m1

p1.role: Meta Q2 2026 capex including finance-lease principal ($31.08B), the base for sequential growth

a1.role: Q3 2026 sequential growth factor over Q2 2026

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: apply a historical Q3 sequential step-up to the most recent actual quarter. Anchored on p1; the growth factor a1 is centered slightly above the historical ~1.14x Q3 step-up given the steeper 2026 ramp, but below the ~1.30x implied by consensus. Failure mode: if the AI buildout causes a step-change beyond historical seasonality, this understates.

methods.label: m2

p120.role: Meta H1 2026 capex including finance-lease principal ($50.92B), used with FY guidance to derive H2

methods.rationale: Guidance-implied route: FY2026 guidance midpoint (~$137.5B) minus H1 actual ($50.92B) gives H2 capex; multiply by Q3's historical share of H2. Uses p120 and a2. Failure mode: guidance range is wide ($130-145B) and the Q3/Q4 split is uncertain; a Q4 back-end load would lower the estimate.

methods.label: m3

p64.role: Meta Q3 2025 capex including finance-lease principal ($19.37B), the year-ago base

a3.role: Q3 2026 capex as a multiple of Q3 2025 capex

methods.rationale: YoY-growth route: apply a YoY multiple to Q3 2025 capex. The multiple a3 is centered near 2.0x, consistent with the FY2026 guidance-implied growth (~1.8-2.0x) and the ~$40B consensus (~2.1x). Failure mode: if YoY growth decelerates or accelerates materially from the full-year trajectory, this misses.

methods.label: m4

p157.role: Analyst consensus Q3 2026 capex including finance leases ($40.5B, S&P Global Market Intelligence)

methods.rationale: Consensus route: use the S&P Global Market Intelligence consensus figure ($40.5B) directly. This is the most credible single consensus point (better provenance than the zhenzhuo $40.97B). Failure mode: consensus may embed an acceleration that does not materialize, or may be stale; it conflicts with the base-rate trajectory (~$33-36B).
